items.title: How Russia's parliamentary election might affect the war in Ukraine
items.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks Russian foreign policy expert Hanna Notte about the results of Russia's parliamentary election and what it means for Moscow's war in Ukraine.

items.title: Why can’t the UN stop wars?
items.description: The UN was created to help save the world from war. More than 80 years later, conflicts and atrocities continue.

items.title: Gaza's women are the only ones keeping their families alive: 'I had to keep going to find food for the children'
items.description: The war waged by Israel has upended the structures of families in Gaza, where women now head nearly one in four households. Tens of thousands of Palestinian women have been left alone to feed their children and seek help and shelter in a dangerous environment.

items.title: Largest attack on Moscow sees Ukraine fire hundreds of drones, mayor says
items.description: Moscow's mayor says 450 drones were downed during the overnight barrage, in which two people died.

items.title: Russian Election, Cast as Test of Support for Ukraine War, Enters Final Day
items.description: A parliamentary election that Putin has cast as a test of support for the war in Ukraine entered its third day, with the ruling United Russia party expected to retain its dominance.

items.title: Why Houthi offensive in Yemen has implications for Mideast and global trade
items.description: The Houthis in Yemen have captured strategic parts of the country, disrupting Saudi oil exports, threatening the global energy trade.

items.title: Trump Signs Russia-Iran Sanctions Bill, Putting New Pressure Tools At His Disposal
items.description: US President Donald Trump signed into law legislation aimed at increasing economic pressure on Russia over its war on Ukraine, including by targeting Moscow's energy revenues as well as countries that continue to buy Russian oil and gas.

items.title: Yemeni militants: How powerful are the Houthis now?
items.description: After Houthi victories in Yemen, the group's importance in the US-Iran war has grown. Previously Lebanon's Hezbollah was considered most significant in Iran's "axis of resistance." Now the Houthis are rising to the top.

items.title: Sexual violence against civilians and POW’s in Ukraine widespread and ‘abhorrent’
items.description: Over 1,000 cases of sexual violence against civilians and prisoners of war (POWs) in Ukraine have been documented from the start of Russia’s invasion to the end of July this year.
